newsitem.title: USA: World Trade Center blast victim testifies.
newsitem.headline: World Trade Center blast victim testifies.

text.p: A victim of the World Trade Centre bombing testified on Wednesday against the accused mastermind Ramzi Yousef, recalling how he feared he had gone blind in the moments after the devasting blast.
Timothy Lang, a stockbroker, said he was standing in the underground parking garage on Feb. 26, 1993, when an explosion rocked the 110-floor twin towers.

"I was lifted into the air and thrown directly away from my car. Something hit me in the head," he said. "When I woke up, I was lying on my back. The first thing I noticed, it was pitch black. I was afraid I was blind."

Lang was one of several witnesses to testify on Wednesday in the trial of the two Moslem militants -- Yousef, who is accused of building and planting the bomb, and Eyad Ismoil, who is accused of driving the van that carried the device into the building's garage.
Prosecutors say they were part of a war of terrorism against the United States and wanted to kill thousands of people to retaliate for U.S. support for Israel.
The blast killed six people, injured more than 1,000 and caused more than $550 million in damages.
Employees of the New York and New Jersey Port Authority, which oversees the World Trade Centre complex, also testified.

Among witnesses due to appear on Thursday was a Port Authority official who is expected to identify the four Port Authority employees killed in the blast -- Monica Smith, William Macko, Robert Kirkpatrick and Steven Knapp.
A fifth victim, Wilfredo Mercado, worked at the Vista Hotel adjacent to the twin towers, and the sixth victim was John DiGiovanni, a dental salesman.
Lang said he had followed a silver Ford in the garage, and that he and the driver of the Ford had waited several minutes for a parking space. He identified the driver as DiGiovanni.
"If he hadn't cut me off going down the ramp, I'd have gotten his parking spot and I wouldn't be here today," Lang testified.
The two defendants stared directly at Lang but showed no emotion as he described getting to his feet, groping his way through the smoke and darkness and finding the garage exits blocked by rubble.
"I became terrified," he said. "I realised I was helpless. The smoke was so thick. I couldn't save myself and so I began to pray."
"After a while, I became calm and I realised I would have to lie there until I was either rescued or died," he said. He was bleeding from a head wound, he said.
After screaming for help, he said, the next thing he remembered was being lifted by two men, carried out and given oxygen.
Four other Moslem fundamentalists were convicted on charges stemming from the bombing in 1994, and each was sentenced to 240 years in prison.
Yousef and Ismoil fled the country the night of the explosion. Yousef was captured in Pakistan in 1995 and Ismoil was arrested in Jordan last year.
